primary_pixels: Full 1080 × 810 civic-3-4 frame, x from left and y from top. Reported corners are the fitted frame perimeter at the glazing face (not roof/under-sill masonry). Manual uncertainty generally 1–2 px; 3–6 px at lower, leaf-obscured glazing. Line positions are rounded observations, not a universal straight-world-wall fit.

observed_windows.label: western inner wide bay, fourth floor
observed_windows.observability: Six columns and five rows, the main transom below the top two rows. Window heads follow a slightly tilted line in the image. Civic-3-1 is an independent close detail of the lower casements and paired upper lights.

observed_windows.label: western inner wide bay, third floor
observed_windows.observability: The third and fourth floors use the same wide frame. Trees cover several neighbouring bays. The central mullion and lower casement edges are heavier than the fine upper bars.

observed_windows.label: central three narrow openings, fourth floor
observed_windows.observability: Middle of three. Two vertical rods per opening produce three columns, and the heavy rail is in the middle. Adjacent jambs of the centre window are masonry.

observed_windows.label: central three narrow openings, third floor
observed_windows.observability: Middle opening repeated each side of it. Lower casement edges are resolvable.

observed_windows.label: central three narrow openings, second floor
observed_windows.observability: Each opening has four columns. The heavy rail near the foot also appears in the independent oblique view pic-17. The section widths remain approximate.

observed_windows.label: western inner wide bay, second floor
observed_windows.observability: Repeated dark metal lines measured at three scan heights in the top register. Heavier uprights at columns three and seven bound wider central sash. The middle band below the main rail shows fine divisions on the clearer east side of this bay. The bottom register uses three wide panels; tree reflections cover its two lower corners.

observed_windows.label: western inner wide bay, ground
observed_windows.observability: The outer four points enclose the whole bay provisionally. Two pale masonry piers split it into narrow, broad and narrow clear holes. The right-hand counterpart in pic-17 shows the piers, transom glass and lower glazing; trees and shop signs cover other bays. Individual current shop fittings are outside the modelled steel-window scope.

unobstructed_window_counts.wide_second: 10 upper columns with heavy breaks at 3 and 7; 3 full lower panels, two principal horizontal boundaries.

ground: Two massive pale mullions in each evidenced ground bay remain with masonry. Side lights and a wider central light are modeled behind the apertures; no uniform evidence for handles or mechanisms behind the shop signs and vegetation.
photography_rights: Photographs used for observation. No image pixels are reproduced in these glazing materials. All geometry and the tile are original metric constructions. The bridge photographs predate the current refurbishment.
